newsitem.title: UK: Rain too little to solve long term UK problem.
newsitem.headline: Rain too little to solve long term UK problem.

text.p: The weekend's rain has not been enough to alleviate the long term supply problem in East Anglia, one of Britain's most important cereals producing areas, according to the Environment Agency.
"It's just not sufficient rain to resolve a long term problem, an East Anglian based spokeswoman for the agency, which controls the abstraction of water by farmers for irrigation, told Reuters.
"The rain wasn't enough to replenish ground water supplies," after a two year spell of dry weather, she said.
Some groups of farmers had already agreed to restrict water use, ahead of possible more widespread controls, she said.
Between Friday and Sunday, 18 millimetres of rain fell on south-eastern England, the London Weather Centre said. Most of Northern Ireland, England and Wales had rain, a spokesman said.
